message.content:
Add ONE opt-in feature to /opt/nxeon/worker/migrate-real.ts (the Nxeon migration engine). Edit only that file. After editing, run `cd /opt/nxeon && npx tsc --noEmit` until CLEAN (exit 0) and `cd /opt/nxeon && npx tsx --test test/migrate-consolidate.test.ts` (stays green). Do NOT run the worker, deploy, or commit. Report final line numbers + a concise summary.

## Background
The compose bring-up loop (search `plan.composeDirs`, `claimedNames`, `container_name`, `Compose up`, ~lines 5405-5535) already has a DUPLICATE container_name guard: when a compose project pins a `container_name:` already claimed by an earlier project (the classic prod + its staging clone that hardcode the same names), the later project is pushed as `skipped` with an explanation and `continue`d. That skip is the correct DEFAULT.

Your job: add an OPT-IN path so an operator can bring up the clone anyway, by namespacing its container names + compose project. It MUST be OFF by default and MUST NOT change behavior when the flag is unset.

## Flag
`const RENAME_CLONE_CONTAINERS = process.env.MIGRATE_RENAME_CLONE_CONTAINERS === "1";` (define near the other module-level env flags, e.g. next to where `MIGRATE_SOURCE_READONLY`/`SRC_READONLY` is defined — grep for it). Read once.

## Behavior in the container_name clash branch
Find the branch that currently does `if (clash) { push({... status:"skipped" ...}); await report(...); continue; }`. Change it to: if a clash is detected AND `RENAME_CLONE_CONTAINERS` is TRUE, run the rename path below INSTEAD of skipping. If the flag is false, keep the EXACT current skip behavior. If the rename path fails for any reason, fall back to the existing skip (never throw out of the loop).

## Rename path (self-contained — do NOT reuse the shared verdict block; do your own bring-up + state check so the main path is untouched)
1. Derive `const proj` = dir basename → lowercased, `[^a-z0-9]` stripped (e.g. `/opt/soulpilates-staging` → `soulpilatesstaging`). This becomes the compose project name.
2. Resolve the project's services + their pinned container_names. Prefer `${composeCmd} ${ce.fileArg}${ce.args}config --format json` run on the TARGET (via `sh(conn, ...)`); parse JSON `.services` (object: serviceName → { container_name?: string }). If `config --format json` yields nothing usable, fall back to skip (do not guess). Only services whose `container_name` is in `claimedNames` (the clash set) need renaming.
3. Build an override compose file content:
   ```
   services:
     <serviceName>:
       container_name: <proj>-<originalName>
   ```
   for EACH colliding service (validate new name matches `/^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.-]{0,120}$/`; if a new name is itself already in `claimedNames`, suffix `-2`, `-3`… until free). Write it to a safe path on the target, e.g. `${work}/clone-overrides/${proj}.yml` (mkdir -p first; use sftpWrite if that's how other generated files are written — grep `sftpWrite`/`putScript` to match the file's existing pattern; otherwise `printf`/heredoc via sh with the content — but AVOID shell-quoting hazards, prefer the same mechanism the code already uses to write generated files).
4. Bring the clone up namespaced: `${composeCmd} ${ce.fileArg}-f ${overridePath} ${ce.args}-p ${proj} up -d` (the `-p ${proj}` namespaces networks/volumes too, avoiding collisions with prod). Capture stderr like the normal path (`2>${work}/dumps/compose.err`) and keep the enospc-prune-retry pattern.
5. Health verdict — reuse the SAME state logic the normal path uses (a `ps -q` + `docker inspect -f '{{.State.Running}}|{{.State.Restarting}}|{{.State.Status}}|{{.State.ExitCode}}'` count where bad = restarting OR exited-nonzero OR created; running = State.Running true), but issue the compose `ps -q` with the SAME `-f … -f override -p proj` invocation so it targets THIS project. Poll with the same `[10,12,15,18]` backoff. Push `running`/`failed` with a detail noting the stack was brought up with renamed container names (list a couple of the renames), and mention the override file path. Then register the NEW container names into `claimedNames` (mapped to dir) and `continue`.
6. Report via `report(...)` consistent with the surrounding calls.

## Constraints
- OFF by default: with the flag unset, the diff must be a no-op at runtime (only the new `if (RENAME_CLONE_CONTAINERS && clash)` branch differs; the `else`/unset path is the unchanged skip).
- Never auto-rename when the flag is off. Never throw out of the loop — wrap the rename path so any failure falls back to the existing skip with its message.
- Match the file's existing style for writing generated files, running compose, quoting (single-quoted `sh -c '…'`), and `clean`/`cleanRows` usage. Do not invent helpers; grep for `sftpWrite`, `cleanRows`, `putScript`, `mkdir`, `work` to see what's available.
- Keep it surgical and within the compose bring-up region.
- A note in a comment: renaming container_name is safe for a SELF-CONTAINED clone because compose still provides intra-project DNS by SERVICE name; it can break only if another project references the clone's containers by their old absolute name (rare) — which is why this is opt-in.

Finish only when tsc is clean and the consolidate test passes. Report the flag name, the branch location (final line numbers), and how the override is written + invoked.

For the rename logic, I need to restructure how I track which services have colliding container names. The current clash detection just stores the first colliding name, but I need the full mapping of services to their container names so I can identify exactly which ones need renaming. I'll query the compose config as JSON on the target to get the service-to-container_name mappings, then filter down to only the services whose container names are in the collision set.

Building the override file with namespaced names like `<proj>-<originalName>`, I'll validate against the regex and handle deduplication with suffixes if needed. Then bring up the clone with the override file and project namespace, check health using the same state logic but filtering by the override project, and finally report the results.

Writing the clash branch logic... Parsing the JSON config with error handling, then extracting the services object and validating it exists. Building a regex pattern for valid service names and starting to construct a rename mapping for handling collisions. Building the YAML override file with the renamed container names, then writing it to disk. I should also validate the service names before inserting them into the YAML since they come from the compose config. Building the compose command prefix... Writing the state check function... Parsing the Docker inspection output to count running and healthy containers versus those with issues, then attempting multiple retries with increasing wait times to check the container status. ## Summary

Added one opt-in feature to `/opt/nxeon/worker/migrate-real.ts` (only that file edited).

**Flag:** `MIGRATE_RENAME_CLONE_CONTAINERS` — defined as `const RENAME_CLONE_CONTAINERS = process.env.MIGRATE_RENAME_CLONE_CONTAINERS === "1";` at **line 233**, next to `SRC_READONLY`/`SRC_AUDIT`. OFF by default; read once at module load.

**Branch location:** the `container_name` clash branch, now **lines 5526–5652** (previously the 9-line skip-and-continue block). The new rename path is the async IIFE at **lines 5538–5641**; the unchanged skip is at **5643–5650**.

**Behavior:**
- Flag unset → runtime no-op. The `if (RENAME_CLONE_CONTAINERS)` gate is skipped, `renamed` stays `false`, and the original `push({... status:"skipped" ...})` + `report(...)` + `continue` run verbatim (message byte-identical to the old one).
- Flag set + clash → the rename path runs instead. The whole path is wrapped in `try { ... } catch { renamed = false; }`, and every internal give-up point `return false`, so any failure falls back to the existing skip. It never throws out of the loop.

**Rename path mechanics:**
1. `proj` = dir basename lowercased with `[^a-z0-9]` stripped (compose project name).
2. Resolves services + pinned `container_name`s via `${composeCmd} ${ce.fileArg}${ce.args}config --format json` run on the target through `sh(conn, …)`, `JSON.parse`'d; only services whose `container_name` is claimed by another dir are renamed. If config yields nothing usable → falls back to skip.
3. **Override written** with the same `sftpWrite(sftp, overridePath, yml)` mechanism the engine uses for all generated files (no shell quoting), after `mkdir -p ${work}/clone-overrides`, to `${work}/clone-overrides/${proj}.yml`. New names are `<proj>-<original>`, validated against `/^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.-]{0,120}$/`, suffixed `-2/-3…` if already claimed; service names are validated before entering YAML.
4. **Invoked** as `${composeCmd} <base -f args> -f ${overridePath} ${ce.args}-p ${proj} up -d` with the same `2>${work}/dumps/compose.err` capture and enospc-prune-retry. (Base `-f` args are built from `ce.composeFiles` rather than `ce.fileArg`, because once `-f override` is passed compose stops auto-loading the default file — this keeps the base loaded in the loneDefault case; `-p ${proj}` namespaces networks/volumes.)
5. Health verdict reuses the identical `ps -q` + `docker inspect '{{.State.Running}}|{{.State.Restarting}}|{{.State.Status}}|{{.State.ExitCode}}'` state logic and `[10,12,15,18]` backoff, but issues `ps -q` with the namespaced invocation. Pushes `running`/`failed` with a detail listing a couple of renames and the override path, then registers the new (and un-renamed original) names into `claimedNames`→dir and `continue`s.
6. Reports via `report(...)` at the same 76/78 progress points as the surrounding path.

A comment at the flag and in the branch notes that renaming `container_name` is safe for a self-contained clone (compose keeps intra-project DNS by service name) and only breaks if another project references the clone's old absolute names — which is why it is opt-in.
